title: 崖の上のポニョ (Gake no Ue no Ponyo — Ponyo on the Cliff)
description:
The ending theme of Studio Ghibli's 2008 film 崖の上のポニョ (Ponyo on the Cliff by the Sea), directed by Hayao Miyazaki. Lyrics by 近藤勝也 and 宮崎駿, music by 久石譲 (Joe Hisaishi), performed by 藤岡藤巻と大橋のぞみ — a duo pairing veteran folk musician 藤岡藤巻 with then-8-year-old 大橋のぞみ in her singing debut. The song became a massive cultural phenomenon in Japan, spending weeks at the top of the Oricon charts and becoming instantly recognisable to every Japanese person.

The lyrics are written entirely from the perspective of Ponyo herself — a goldfish-girl who wants to become human. The vocabulary is deliberately simple: the song was written for a child performer to sing and for children to understand. Almost every word is N5 level. The repetition of 'ポーニョ ポーニョ ポニョ' and 'さかなの子' (fish child) makes it one of the most earworm-friendly Japanese songs for new learners.

Key vocabulary: 崖 (cliff), 海 (sea / ocean), さかな (fish), 女の子 (girl), まんまる (perfectly round), 大好き (love / really like), やってきた (came / arrived), 人間 (human being), なりたい (want to become). The contrast between 'さかなの子' and 'にんげんの子' is the song's emotional core.
